hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-01.title: Bound and construction
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-01.body:
A finalist wins the bracket half containing him, which has $8$ players, so he is better than the other $7$ players of his half. Hence at least $7$ players are weaker than every finalist, and the $7$ weakest players can never reach the final: at most $16-7=9$ players can.

Every one of the $9$ best can do it: put that player in one half of the bracket together with the $7$ weakest players, and put the other $8$ of the top $9$ in the other half. He is the best in his half, so he wins it and reaches the final. The answer is $9$.

**Answer: 9**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-02.title: Sum by rounds
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-02.body:
In round $k$ ($k=1,2,3,4$) there are $8,4,2,1$ winners, and each has his $k$th ceremony of $10k$ seconds. Total: $8\cdot10+4\cdot20+2\cdot30+1\cdot40=80+80+60+40=260$ seconds.

**Answer: 260**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-03.title: Area bound
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-03.body:
Place the targeted dragoon at the origin. A dragoon firing at it has its centre in $[-6,6]^2$, so its square lies inside $[-6.5,6.5]^2$, a square of side $13$ and area $169$. The unit squares have disjoint interiors, so at most $169$ fit, one of which is the target itself: at most $168$ shooters. This is achieved by tiling the $13\times13$ region with unit squares centred at the integer points.

**Answer: 168**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-04.title: Timeline
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-04.body:
At time $t$ there are $\lfloor t\rfloor$ zerglings and $\lfloor t/2.1\rfloor$ zealots; the zerg army overpowers when zerglings $>3\cdot$ zealots.

- From $t=1$ (first zergling) to $t=2.1$ (first zealot) there are zerglings and no zealots: $1.1$ minutes.
- With $k$ zealots (present during $[2.1k,\,2.1(k+1))$) the zerglings must number at least $3k+1$, which happens from $t=3k+1$ on. For $k=1$ this is $t=4$, inside $[2.1,4.2)$: another $0.2$ minutes. For $k\ge2$ we have $3k+1\ge2.1(k+1)$, so the next zealot appears before the zerglings catch up, and the zerg army never overpowers again.

Total: $1.1+0.2=1.3$ minutes.

**Answer: 1.3 minutes**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-05.title: Count unordered teams, then order
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-05.body:
After one season the roster contains at least $10$ of the original $11$ players and at most one new player. A lineup of five uses either no new player: $\binom{11}5=462$ choices; or one new player ($100$ choices of who, since $111-11=100$) and four of the original eleven: $100\cdot\binom{11}4=100\cdot330=33000$ choices. (Each such team is achievable: drop one of the original players not used and add the new one.) Total unordered lineups: $33462$. Order matters, so multiply by $5!=120$: $33462\cdot120=4015440$.

**Answer: 4015440**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-06.title: Set up the equation
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-06.body:
The probability of the same side twice is $p^2+(1-p)^2=2p^2-2p+1$; of one of each is $2p(1-p)$. The condition is $2p^2-2p+1=2\cdot2p(1-p)=4p-4p^2$, i.e. $6p^2-6p+1=0$, so $p=\frac{3\pm\sqrt3}6$. The larger is $\frac{3+\sqrt3}6$.

**Answer: $\frac{3+\sqrt3}6$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-07.title: Bayes
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-07.body:
$P(\text{two heads and double-headed})=\frac12\cdot1=\frac12$. $P(\text{two heads})=\frac12\cdot1+\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac58$. So the conditional probability is $\frac{1/2}{5/8}=\frac45$.

**Answer: $\frac45$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-07.title: Compare the two cases
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-07.body:
Before seeing the flips, "double-headed and HH" has probability $\frac12\cdot1=\frac12$ and "fair and HH" has probability $\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac18$. These are in ratio $4:1$, so given HH the coin is double-headed with probability $\frac45$.

**Answer: $\frac45$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-08.title: Binomial
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-08.body:
More heads than tails means $3,4$ or $5$ heads: $\binom53\left(\frac23\right)^3\left(\frac13\right)^2+\binom54\left(\frac23\right)^4\frac13+\left(\frac23\right)^5=\frac{80+80+32}{243}=\frac{192}{243}=\frac{64}{81}$.

**Answer: $\frac{64}{81}$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-09.title: Geometric series
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-09.body:
Newton wins on flip $2n+1$ when the first $2n$ flips alternate in the pattern tails (Newton), heads (Leibniz), repeated $n$ times, and then Newton flips heads: probability $\big((1-p)p\big)^n\,p$. So $P(\text{Newton wins})=\frac{p}{1-p(1-p)}$. Setting this equal to $\frac12$: $2p=1-p+p^2$, so $p^2-3p+1=0$ and $p=\frac{3-\sqrt5}2$ (the other root exceeds $1$).

**Answer: $\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-09.title: Recursive
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-09.body:
Let $N$ be Newton's winning probability. He wins at once with probability $p$. If he flips tails, Leibniz flips: if tails Leibniz wins; if heads (probability $p$) the game restarts. So $N=p+(1-p)p\,N$, giving $N=\frac{p}{1-p+p^2}$ and the same equation as above.

**Answer: $\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-10.title: Parity of changes
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-10.body:
Call a flip a *change* if it differs from the previous flip; each of the $2010$ flips is a change independently with probability $\frac13$. The last flip is heads exactly when the number of changes is even. With $p=\frac23$ (no change) and $q=\frac13$ (change), $P(\text{even})=\frac{(p+q)^{2010}+(p-q)^{2010}}2=\frac{1+(1/3)^{2010}}2$.

So the probability is $\frac{3^{2010}+1}{2\cdot3^{2010}}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{3^{2010}+1}{2\cdot3^{2010}}$**

hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-10.title: Recurrence
hmmt-nov-2010-gen2-10.body:
Let $h_n$ be the probability that flip number $n$ is heads, with $h_0=1$. Then $h_{n+1}=\frac23h_n+\frac13(1-h_n)=\frac13h_n+\frac13$, so $h_{n+1}-\frac12=\frac13\left(h_n-\frac12\right)$. Hence $h_{2010}=\frac12+\frac12\cdot3^{-2010}=\frac{3^{2010}+1}{2\cdot3^{2010}}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{3^{2010}+1}{2\cdot3^{2010}}$**
